content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Supplier Concentration Fragility", "construction": "From annual 10-K disclosures under SFAS 131, identify firms that report dependence on one or more major suppliers accounting for 10%+ of purchases (parsed from text). Construct a dummy = 1 if the firm reports a concentrated supplier base, refined by counting the number of named critical suppliers scaled inversely. Combine with inventory-to-COGS ratio to proxy buffer capacity. Rank cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "Firms reliant on few suppliers face under-priced disruption risk; investors underweight the tail risk of input shocks, requiring a return premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high supplier concentration (few critical suppliers, low inventory buffer)"}, {"name": "Deferred Revenue Momentum", "construction": "Using quarterly balance-sheet deferred revenue (current + long-term), compute the year-over-year growth rate in deferred revenue scaled by total assets. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter on the four-quarter trend in this ratio.", "rationale": "Growth in deferred revenue reflects contracted but unrecognized future sales, a leading indicator of demand that is slow to be incorporated into prices.", "higher_returns_for": "high deferred revenue growth"}, {"name": "Working Capital Acceleration", "construction": "Compute non-cash net working capital (receivables + inventory - payables) scaled by sales for each of the last 8 quarters. Fit the second difference (acceleration) of this ratio. Rank firms on the acceleration term, controlling for level and first difference via cross-sectional regression residuals each quarter.", "rationale": "Accelerating working capital signals deteriorating operational efficiency and unsustainable growth financing that the market prices with a lag.", "higher_returns_for": "low (most negative) working capital acceleration"}, {"name": "Analyst Coverage Dispersion Decay", "construction": "From I/B/E/S detail files, measure the month-over-month change in the standard deviation of individual analyst FY1 EPS estimates, scaled by price. Compute the 3-month change in dispersion. Rank firms cross-sectionally on the decline (convergence) of estimates.", "rationale": "Converging analyst estimates signal resolving information uncertainty; as ambiguity resolves favorably, prices drift upward before full incorporation.", "higher_returns_for": "large decline in estimate dispersion"}, {"name": "Capital Expenditure Text Intensity", "construction": "Parse the MD&A section of 10-K filings for frequency of forward-looking capex and expansion language (terms like 'expand capacity', 'new facility', 'capital investment') normalized by document length. Combine with realized capex/assets to form a residual of 'talk vs. spend'. Rank firms each June.", "rationale": "Firms that announce expansion intentions beyond realized spending exhibit managerial overconfidence and overinvestment, predicting lower future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low text-to-spend residual (spending exceeds announced intentions)"}, {"name": "Seasonal Earnings Persistence Gap", "construction": "For each firm, regress quarterly earnings on the same-quarter earnings one year prior over a rolling 5-year window to estimate seasonal persistence. Separately estimate adjacent-quarter persistence. Rank firms on the gap (seasonal minus adjacent persistence coefficient).", "rationale": "Firms with strong seasonal but weak sequential earnings persistence have predictable earnings the market under-anticipates in specific quarters.", "higher_returns_for": "high seasonal persistence gap ahead of strong quarters"}, {"name": "Intangible-Adjusted Asset Growth", "construction": "Capitalize R&D and a fraction of SG&A as intangible assets using perpetual-inventory method with standard amortization rates, add to reported total assets. Compute year-over-year growth of this adjusted asset base. Rank firms cross-sectionally each June.", "rationale": "The classic asset-growth anomaly ignores intangible investment; adjusting reveals that firms growing true (tangible+intangible) capital fastest overinvest and underperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low intangible-adjusted asset growth"}, {"name": "Debt Maturity Wall Proximity", "construction": "From Compustat debt maturity schedule (debt due in years 1-5), compute the share of total debt maturing within the next 12 months, scaled by cash plus operating cash flow. Rank firms cross-sectionally each quarter.", "rationale": "Firms facing imminent large refinancing relative to liquidity bear rollover risk that is under-priced outside of crisis periods, commanding a premium.", "higher_returns_for": "high near-term maturity relative to liquidity"}, {"name": "Order Backlog Surprise", "construction": "Using reported order backlog (Compustat item OB) scaled by sales, compute the change relative to its own 3-year average and relative to the seasonal norm. Rank firms cross-sectionally on positive backlog surprises each fiscal period.", "rationale": "Backlog is a forward demand signal disclosed by manufacturers that receives limited investor attention, generating post-disclosure drift.", "higher_returns_for": "high positive backlog surprise"}, {"name": "Gross Margin Volatility Compression", "construction": "Compute the rolling 12-quarter standard deviation of quarterly gross margin (gross profit/sales). Measure the ratio of recent 4-quarter volatility to the trailing 12-quarter volatility. Rank firms on the compression (recent volatility falling relative to history).", "rationale": "Declining margin volatility signals stabilizing competitive position and pricing power, a fundamental improvement priced with delay.", "higher_returns_for": "high margin volatility compression (stabilizing margins)"}]}
